answer: In the zone of indifference, a distinction is established between the forces that generate Lust and those that generate Unlust. Specifically, the zone separates experiences that lead to pleasure from those that lead to displeasure, establishing a polarity within the realm of desire.

answer: The singularity of the analytic experience relates to the unique nature of the experience itself when it pertains to Freud. It suggests that the analytic experience is not replicable in a concrete reality, implying a specific, irreducible quality to how Freud behaved in his work. This singularity highlights the ineffable nature of the analytic process.

They are the best introduction we have to the manner in which Freud behaved. But it really does seem as if the character of this experience cannot be reproduced in its concrete reality. answer: The inverted bouquet illustrates the intricate relationship between the imaginary and the real within the psychic economy. It demonstrates how the structure of the imaginary world interacts with the real world, showing how these two realms are intricately intertwined. The experiment serves to show the consequence of this intrication on psychic operations.

contexts.text: This is a fable we will put to a great deal of use. To be sure, this schema has no pretension to touch on anything which has a substantial relation to anything we deal with in analysis, the so-called real or objective relations, or the imaginary relations. But it allows us to illustrate in a particularly simple way what follows on from the strict intrication of the imaginary world and the real world in the psychic economy — now you are going to see how. This little experiment pleased me. It is not me who invented it, it has been around for a long time, known as the experiment of the inverted bouquet. As it

The bouquet is reflected in the spherical surface, meeting at the symmetrical point of luminosity. Consequently, a real image is formed. Note that the rays do not quite cross perfectly in my schema, but that is also true in reality, and for all optical instruments — one only ever gets an approximation. Beyond the eye, the rays continue their movement, and diverge once again. But for the eye, they are convergent, and give a real image, since the characteristic of rays which strike the eye in a convergent form is that they give a real image. Convergent in meeting the eye, they diverge in moving away from it. If the rays happen to meet the eye in the opposite sense, then a virtual image is formed. This is what happens when you look at an image in the mirror — you see it where it isn’t. Here, on the contrary, you see it where it is —on the one condition that your eye be in the field of the rays which have already crossed each other at the corresponding point.
